examples.ko: 첫돌 때 받은 금반지를 지금도 서랍에 보관하고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the gold ring I received on my first birthday in a drawer.
The price of a gold ring changes depending on the price of gold.
The gold ring is too small and won't go on my finger.

examples.ko: 결혼 선물로 금반지 한 쌍을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pair of gold rings as a wedding gift.
I asked them to engrave a name on the gold ring.
Both a gold ring and a silver ring suit you well.

explain: 금으로 만든 반지예요. 한국에서는 아기의 첫돌에 선물하는 금반지를 '돌반지'라고 따로 불러요. 짝말로 '은반지'가 있고, 동사는 '끼다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother went to the market wearing a gold ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반지를 손가락에 착용할 때는 동사 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb 끼다 is used for wearing a ring on a finger.

phrases.en: Silver rings are cheaper than gold rings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금 대신 은으로 만든 반지로, 금반지의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ring made of silver instead of gold; the counterpart to 금반지.

phrases.en: I gave my nephew a gold ring for his first birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기의 첫돌에 선물하는 금반지만 따로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A special name for the gold ring given for a baby's first birthday.

explain_en: It is a ring made of gold. In Korea, the gold ring given as a gift on a baby's first birthday has its own name, '돌반지'. Its counterpart is '은반지' (silver ring), and the verb is '끼다' (to wear).

examples.en: The back of my hair was flattened, so I wore a hat.
Check the shape of the back of your hair in the mirror.

examples.ko: 샤워 후라서 뒷머리는 아직 안 말랐어요.
examples.en: I just showered, so the back of my hair isn't dry yet.
At the salon I only had the back of my hair trimmed a little.
Shall I braid the back of your younger sibling's hair nicely?
Someone stuck gum in the back of my hair.

explain: 머리 뒤쪽의 머리카락이에요. 머리 뒷부분 자체는 '뒤통수'예요. 짝이 되는 '앞머리'는 보통 이마를 덮는 짧은 머리를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: I tied my back hair into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 모양을 말할 때 '묶다'와 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 묶다 (to tie) when talking about hairstyles.

phrases.en: I got the back of my hair cut short at the hair salon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미용실 이야기에서 '자르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 자르다 (to cut) when talking about the hair salon.

phrases.en: The front hair is short and the back hair is long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말 '앞머리'와 같이 쓰면 머리 모양을 비교할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with its counterpart 앞머리 to compare parts of a hairstyle.

explain_en: This is the hair at the back of the head. The back of the head itself is '뒤통수'. The counterpart '앞머리' usually means the short hair over the forehead, like bangs.

examples.ko: 이 가방에는 유명한 회사 마크가 있어요.
examples.en: This bag has a famous company's logo on it.

examples.ko: 지도에 별 마크를 붙인 곳이 우리 집이에요.
examples.en: The place I marked with a star on the map is my house.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 가슴에 작은 하트 마크가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: This shirt has a small heart mark on the chest.
I always check the recycling mark on the packaging.

examples.ko: 앱 아이콘에 빨간 마크가 생기면 새 알림이 온 거예요.
examples.en: When a red mark appears on the app icon, a new notification has come.

examples.ko: 이 마크의 뜻을 아는 사람 있어요?
examples.en: Does anyone know what this mark means?

explain: 작은 그림이나 표시에 써요. '하트 마크', '별 마크', '재활용 마크'처럼 앞에 모양이나 이름이 붙어요. 회사의 상징은 '로고'도 많이 써요. 축구에서 상대 선수를 막는 '마크하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: There is a heart mark next to the message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양 이름 뒤에 '마크'를 붙여서 작은 그림을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 마크 after a shape name to refer to a small symbol.

phrases.en: The bottle has a recycling mark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 붙은 약속된 표시를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for standard symbols printed on products.

phrases.en: I put a check mark on the correct answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞는 답이나 끝낸 일에 표시하는 ✓ 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ✓ shape used to mark a correct answer or a finished task.

explain_en: It is used for small pictures or signs, with a shape or name in front, as in 하트 마크, 별 마크, and 재활용 마크. For a company's symbol, 로고 is also common. In soccer there is also 마크하다, for marking an opposing player.

en: to be discovered; to be found

examples.en: An old letter was found in the drawer.

examples.ko: 공원에서 길을 잃은 강아지가 발견돼서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm glad the lost puppy was found in the park.

examples.ko: 집 근처에서 실종된 아이가 무사히 발견되었어요.
examples.en: The missing child was found safely near home.

examples.ko: 이 병은 일찍 발견되면 치료가 쉬워요.
examples.en: If this illness is detected early, treatment is easy.
I saw news that a new star had been discovered.
No trace of the culprit has been found yet.

explain: 내가 찾아내면 '발견하다', 찾아지는 쪽을 주어로 하면 '발견되다'예요. '찾다'는 일부러 찾는 느낌이고, '발견하다'는 우연히 눈에 띄는 경우에도 써요. 처음 만들어 내는 '발명'과는 달리 이미 있던 것을 알게 되는 거예요.

phrases.en: I found a wallet on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아내는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person who finds it is the subject.

phrases.en: The lost key hasn't been found yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 찾지 못했다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it has not been found yet.

phrases.en: The place where the cat was found is the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발견되다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 장소나 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaches '발견되다' before a noun to talk about a place or time.
phrases.en_equiv: the place where it was found

explain_en: When you find something, it is '발견하다'; when the thing found is the subject, it is '발견되다'. '찾다' feels like searching on purpose, while '발견하다' also fits something that catches your eye by chance. Unlike '발명' (inventing), it means coming to know something that was already there.

examples.ko: 배달부가 문 앞에 음식을 놓고 갔어요.
examples.en: The delivery man left the food at the door.
He worked as a mail carrier for a long time.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 배달부가 더 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: On rainy days delivery workers look busier.

examples.ko: 저는 문 앞에서 배달부에게 감사하다고 인사했어요.
examples.en: At the door I thanked the delivery man.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 배달부는 항상 웃으면서 인사해요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood delivery man always greets us with a smile.
The delivery man rang the doorbell.

explain: 요즘 음식 배달은 '배달 기사님'이나 '라이더', 택배는 '택배 기사님'이라고 많이 불러요. '배달부'는 신문·우편처럼 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 직접 부를 때는 '기사님'이 더 정중해요.

phrases.en: The delivery driver called.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘은 '배달부'보다 '배달 기사님'이라고 더 많이 부르고 더 정중해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nowadays 배달 기사님 is more common than 배달부 and sounds more polite.

phrases.en: The mail carrier brought a letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지나 우편물을 배달하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who delivers letters and mail.

phrases.en: My father was a newspaper delivery boy when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문을 집집마다 배달하는 사람을 말하고, 옛날 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who delivers newspapers house to house, with an old-fashioned feel.

explain_en: For food delivery people now say 배달 기사님 or 라이더, and for parcels 택배 기사님. 배달부 has an older feel, as with newspapers and mail. When calling someone directly, 기사님 is more polite.

examples.en: The kids color nicely in their sketchbooks with crayons.
Yesterday I colored a picture together with my younger sibling.

examples.ko: 저는 그림 속 하늘을 파란색으로 색칠할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to color the sky blue.

examples.ko: 아직 색칠하지 않은 그림이 책상 위에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a picture I haven't colored yet on the desk.
I stuck the picture colored with crayons on the wall.

examples.ko: 제가 그림을 예쁘게 색칠해서 엄마에게 선물했어요.
examples.en: I colored the picture and gave it to Mom as a gift.

explain: '칠하다'는 벽이나 문처럼 색을 바르는 일 전반에 써요. '색칠하다'는 그림이나 도형 안을 색으로 채울 때 특히 자주 써요. 그림 속을 색칠하며 노는 책은 '색칠 공부 책'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father painted the wall white.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칠하다'는 벽이나 문처럼 색을 바르는 일 전체에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Chilhada' covers any kind of applying color, like on walls or doors.

phrases.en: Please color this picture blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to make a request.

phrases.en: My child likes coloring books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림 속을 색칠하며 노는 책을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for a book where you color in pictures.

explain_en: 칠하다 covers applying paint to walls, doors and so on. 색칠하다 is the usual word for filling in a drawing or shape with color. A book you color in is called a '색칠 공부' book.

examples.en: When doing the dishes, I put detergent on the sponge.
This sponge soaks up water well.
The sponge is worn out, so I need to buy a new one.
I wiped the water off the desk with a sponge.
This sponge cake is soft and sweet.

examples.ko: 아이가 스펀지 장난감을 물에 넣고 놀아요.
examples.en: The child plays with a sponge toy in the water.

explain: 부엌에서는 설거지용 스펀지, 욕실에서는 몸을 닦는 스펀지, 화장할 때는 화장 스펀지로 써요. 비유로 '스펀지처럼 빨아들이다'라고 하면 빨리 배우는 사람을 말해요. 비슷한 도구로 '수세미'가 있는데 거친 면이 있는 설거지 도구예요.

phrases.en: I bought a new dish sponge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부엌에서 쓰는 스펀지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the sponge used in the kitchen.

phrases.en: I wipe the bathroom wall with a sponge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 도구로 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(eu)ro' marks the sponge as the tool.

phrases.en: Children learn quickly, like sponges.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유로 쓰면 빨리 배우는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively, it describes learning fast.

explain_en: There are kitchen sponges, bath sponges, and makeup sponges. Figuratively, 스펀지처럼 빨아들이다 describes someone who learns quickly. A similar tool is 수세미, a scrubbing tool with a rougher surface.

examples.en: On the weekend, I bought cool summer clothes at the market.

examples.ko: 여름옷은 땀이 잘 마르는 소재를 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For summer clothes, it's good to choose fabric that dries sweat well.

examples.ko: 겨울이 지나면 옷장에 있는 여름옷부터 꺼내요.
examples.en: When winter passes, I take summer clothes out of the closet first.
My summer clothes are thin, so the air conditioning feels cold.
The price of summer clothes has gone up a lot since last year.

examples.ko: 휴가 갈 때 여름옷 몇 벌만 챙기세요.
examples.en: When you go on vacation, just pack a few summer outfits.

explain: 계절별로 '봄옷, 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷'처럼 말해요. 철이 바뀔 때 옷을 바꿔 정리하는 걸 '옷 정리를 하다'라고 해요. 옷은 '벌'로 세서 '여름옷 세 벌'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 여행 가방에 여름옷 세 벌을 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I put three summer outfits in my travel bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷은 '벌'로 세요. 숫자와 함께 개수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes are counted with 'beol'. Use it to say how many pieces.

phrases.en: It got hot, so I took my summer clothes out of the closet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 바뀔 때 옷을 정리하는 상황에서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said when seasons change and you reorganize your clothes.

phrases.example: 더운 나라에 가서 얇은 여름옷만 입었어요.
phrases.en: I went to a hot country and wore only thin summer clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름옷의 특징을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what kind of summer clothes they are.

explain_en: By season you say '봄옷, 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷'. When the season changes, swapping out your wardrobe is '옷 정리를 하다'. Clothes are counted with '벌', as in '여름옷 세 벌'.

examples.en: We decorate a tree together at Christmas.

examples.ko: 생일 파티를 위해 방을 꽃으로 장식했어요.
examples.en: I decorated the room with flowers for the birthday party.
A cake looks prettier if you decorate it with fruit.
I want to decorate the wall with pictures.

examples.ko: 집을 장식하는 데 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Decorating the house took a long time.
It's the day the students decorated the classroom.

explain: '장식하다'는 '꾸미다'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고, 물건이나 공간에 주로 써요. 사람의 얼굴이나 옷차림에는 '꾸미다'를 써요. 방을 꾸밀 때는 '방을 꾸미다'도 아주 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I decorate my room prettily with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장식하다'보다 쉬운 일상 말이고, 사람의 얼굴이나 옷차림에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word than 장식하다, and it can also be used for a person's looks.

phrases.en: I decorated the table with flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 꾸민 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for something already decorated.

phrases.en: We don't decorate the walls in our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 꾸미지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say you do not decorate.

explain_en: '장식하다' is close to '꾸미다' but more formal and mostly used for objects and spaces. For a person's face or outfit, use '꾸미다'. For a room, '방을 꾸미다' is just as natural.

examples.en: I ran into my teacher as I was passing by the school on my way here.

examples.ko: 어려운 시간을 지나온 만큼 이제는 행복해요.
examples.en: Having come through hard times, I'm happy now.
On the way here, I passed a big market.
After coming through the tunnel, the rain suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 오다가 지나왔는데 문을 닫았더라고요.
examples.en: I passed that shop on my way, and it was closed.

examples.ko: 힘든 시기를 지나와서 이제는 웃을 수 있어요.
examples.en: I've come through a hard period and can smile now.

explain: '지나가다'는 지나서 멀어지는 방향이고, '지나오다'는 어떤 곳을 지나서 지금 있는 쪽으로 오는 방향이에요. '지나온 길', '지나온 세월'처럼 지난 시간을 되돌아볼 때도 써요. 활용은 '지나와요, 지나왔어요, 지나온'이에요.

phrases.en: I looked back at the road I had come along.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-은'을 붙여 이미 지나서 온 곳을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-은' marks a place already passed on the way here.

phrases.en: I just came past the front of the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳을 거쳐서 지금 있는 곳에 왔다는 뜻의 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: passed through a place and arrived where I am now.

phrases.en: It rained on my way back past the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오는 도중에 생긴 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that happened along the way here.

explain_en: '지나가다' moves past and away, while '지나오다' passes something and comes toward where you are now. It's also used to look back on time, as in '지나온 길' (the road traveled) and '지나온 세월' (the years gone by). Forms: '지나와요, 지나왔어요, 지나온'.

examples.en: The casting for the lead was finally announced.

examples.ko: 이 배우는 캐스팅 제안을 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: This actor received many casting offers.
I got approached for casting on the street while walking.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 캐스팅이 좋아서 인기가 많았어요.
examples.en: That drama was popular because its casting was good.

examples.ko: 감독님은 캐스팅할 때 연기를 가장 먼저 봐요.
examples.en: The director looks at acting first when casting.
I failed the casting but I'll try again.

explain: '캐스팅하다'는 감독이나 회사 쪽에서 배역을 정하는 말이고, '캐스팅되다'는 배역을 따낸 사람 쪽에서 해요. 길에서 기획사가 말을 걸 때도 '캐스팅됐다'고 하고, 오디션에서 정해질 때도 같은 말을 써요.

phrases.en: The director cast a new actor as the lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배역을 정하는 감독이나 회사 쪽에서 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb used from the side of the director or company choosing the role.

phrases.en: That new actor was cast in the drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배역을 따낸 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who got the role.

phrases.en: I'm waiting for the movie's casting announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 어떤 배역을 맡는지 알리는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for announcing who will play which role.

explain_en: '캐스팅하다' is said from the director's or agency's side when choosing someone for a role, while '캐스팅되다' is from the side of the person who got the role. Both a street approach by an agency and an audition result are called '캐스팅'.

examples.en: I bought a new phone case.
The color of this case is pretty.
Put your glasses in the case and keep them in the bag.

examples.ko: 케이스가 너무 커서 주머니에 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The case is too big to fit in my pocket.

examples.ko: 이 일은 특별한 케이스라서 먼저 물어봐야 해요.
examples.en: This is a special case, so I have to ask first.
Do I have to buy the charging case too?

explain: 휴대폰·안경·이어폰처럼 물건을 넣거나 씌우는 용품이 '케이스'예요. 휴대폰에 씌우는 건 '커버'라고도 불러요. '이런 경우'라는 뜻으로 '케이스'를 쓰기도 하지만 보통은 '경우'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I put my glasses case in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 넣어 두는 상자나 통을 말할 때 '물건 이름 + 케이스'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'item name + 케이스' for a case that holds that item.

phrases.en: I changed my phone cover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰에 씌우는 것은 '케이스' 대신 '커버'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a phone, people also say 커버 instead of 케이스.

phrases.en: I put a case on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰에 케이스를 끼우는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of putting a case on a phone.

explain_en: A 케이스 is an accessory you put things in or over, like phones, glasses, and earbuds. A phone case is sometimes called a 커버. People also use 케이스 for 'instance', but 경우 is usually more natural.

examples.en: I hung a star on top of the Christmas tree.
The child is busy decorating the Christmas tree.
A huge Christmas tree was set up in front of the church.
I placed a small Christmas tree in the living room.
Little lights twinkled on the Christmas tree.

examples.ko: 백화점 앞 크리스마스트리 옆에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo next to the Christmas tree in front of the department store.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '트리'라고도 해요. '꾸미다, 세우다, 달다'처럼 장식하고 세우는 동사와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I put a small tree in my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크리스마스트리'를 줄인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 크리스마스트리.

phrases.en: I decorated the tree with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장식을 달 때 '꾸미다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 꾸미다 when putting decorations on it.

phrases.en: In December, I set up a tree in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 트리를 처음 놓을 때 '세우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 세우다 when setting the tree up.

explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to just '트리'. It pairs well with verbs for decorating and setting up, such as '꾸미다', '세우다' and '달다'.

examples.en: I wrote a handwritten letter on pretty letter paper.
I ran out of letter paper, so I went to the stationery store.
I bought a pack of flower-patterned letter paper.

examples.ko: 편지지 두 장에 하고 싶은 말을 가득 적었어요.
examples.en: I filled two sheets of letter paper with what I wanted to say.

examples.ko: 이 편지지는 종이가 얇아서 글씨가 비쳐요.
examples.en: This letter paper is thin, so the writing shows through.
I bought the letter paper and envelopes together.

explain: 편지를 쓰는 종이를 말하고, 짝말은 '편지봉투'예요. 보통 문구점에서 '편지지 세트'로 같이 팔아요.

phrases.example: 예쁜 편지지에 친구에게 쓸 편지를 썼어요.
phrases.en: I wrote a letter to my friend on pretty letter paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지를 쓰는 종이를 말할 때 '에'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에 to name the paper you write on.

phrases.en: I bought letter paper and envelopes together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지지와 짝으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The partner word to 편지지.

phrases.en: I got a letter paper set as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문구점에서 묶어서 파는 상품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the bundle sold at stationery stores.

explain_en: This is the paper you write a letter on, and its partner word is '편지봉투' (envelope). They are commonly sold together as a '편지지 세트' at stationery stores.
